title: Two Things Called Attention
scopeNote: This keeps the three stages of the original and above all the hand computation, because how mechanical the operation is does not land from being told. The second sentence where the resolution flips, more of the surrounding architecture, and the longer treatment of interpretability claims stay in the longer version.
summary: Resolve an ambiguous pronoun yourself, then work out by hand the weights a language model would produce over the same sentence, then sort five claims by whether they apply to what you did, to what the model does, to both, or to neither.
learningObjectives: Describe what the operation called attention computes inside a language model.
Explain why a weight distribution over words is not by itself an explanation of an output.
Distinguish resolving a pronoun using world knowledge from reweighting tokens by similarity.
Recognise that a shared name does not imply a shared mechanism.
State what the simplified arithmetic here leaves out of a real model.
interactionTypes: a pronoun resolution the learner makes before any model is mentioned
a hand computation of attention weights from given scores
a live figure of the weights the learner has just worked out
five claims sorted between the two mechanisms, each with an explanation
staged disclosure so no stage is visible before the one before it is done
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every choice is held in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with every choice a labelled button marked with a glyph and a hidden note as well as a colour. Nothing is timed and there is no motion. The scores and the weights appear in a real table as well as in the figure, so the computation can be followed without the graphic, and the figure carries a description listing every weight and stating that they add to one. Each claim's explanation appears as text beneath it whether the learner was right or wrong.
dataStatus: The scores are invented for a five-word illustration and are not taken from any model. The sentence is a standard ambiguous-pronoun example.
simulationNotes: Weights are computed as score divided by the sum of scores. A real model exponentiates before normalising, works over far more tokens, and runs many such weightings in parallel at every layer; plain division keeps the arithmetic doable in the head while preserving what matters here, namely that the weights are a normalised comparison that sums to one because it was divided by its total. The caution states all of this so that nobody leaves thinking they have implemented a transformer. The scores are chosen so the weight does not land overwhelmingly on the referent but spreads across several words including ones with no referential content, which is what a similarity reweighting looks like. The activity does not claim models fail on this sentence, since current models usually resolve it, and it does not take a side on whether attention weights explain outputs, which is genuinely disputed; the caution says so.
readmeTopic: what the operation called attention actually computes, and why sharing a name is not sharing a mechanism
